name: Theta Persei
description: A naked-eye star 11.1 parsecs away, 1.3 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the CHARA Array.

radius.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 16895: radius in solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 1.103 +/- 0.009 mas (CHARA) and the Hipparcos parallax, 1.319 +/- 0.011

mass.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 16895: mass in solar masses, from Yonsei-Yale isochrones at the measured radius and temperature (a model value), 1.138 +/- 0.01

temperature.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 16895: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 6157 +/- 37

distance.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 16895: the Hipparcos parallax the radius was computed with (van Leeuwen 2007), 89.88 +/- 0.23 mas, inverted

text.card: A naked-eye star 11 parsecs away whose disc the CHARA Array measured: 1.3 times the Sun's width.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 1.103 milliarcseconds, which gives 1.319 solar radii and 6,157 K at its surface.
text.locator: Tables 5 and 10, HD 16895: limb-darkened diameter, R, Teff
